## How to Run

```bash
# one-time asset preparation
uv run mlperf fetch --workload time-series-forecasting --profile max

# benchmark run (writes JSON/HTML/CSV reports + .provd provenance)
uv run mlperf run --workload time-series-forecasting --profile max --open-report

# quick smoke pass
uv run mlperf run --workload time-series-forecasting --profile min

# research envelope
uv run mlperf run --workload time-series-forecasting --profile pro
```

See the [running guide](../../guide/running.qmd) for profile semantics, report handling, and power measurement flags.

## Candidate Quality Target

| **Field** | **Value** |
|:---|:---|
| **Metric** | test_mse |
| **Target** | 0.29292929292929293 |
| **Direction** | lower |
| **Target basis** | mlcommons_derived |
| **Tolerance** | 0.0 |
| **Reference runs** | 0 |

**Reviewer notes:**

- The PatchTST paper reports 0.290 MSE, with standard deviation 0.002, for the 336-step context and 96-step forecast horizon.
- MLPerf inference benchmarks commonly require 99% of reference quality. For a lower-is-better error metric, MLPerf EDU applies the direction-aware equivalent, reference MSE divided by 0.99, yielding 0.29292929292929293.
- The derivation is recorded explicitly because applying the MLPerf quality fraction to a lower-is-better metric is an MLPerf EDU policy inference, not a PatchTST-authored threshold.
- The corresponding published MAE is 0.342; it is reported as a secondary metric rather than a second admission gate.
- Promotion still requires every canonical run to meet the derived gate and a committed five-run timing sweep.

| **Included phases** | ETTm1 window loading and device transfer, forward and backward passes, Adam optimizer and OneCycle learning-rate steps, epoch-level validation and test evaluation |
| **Excluded phases** | dataset fetching and CSV parsing, train-split standardization and DataLoader construction, model construction, best-checkpoint serialization, final report and provenance serialization |
| **Device synchronization** | synchronize immediately before and after the measured training-and-evaluation region |

| **Repeatability metric** | train_and_eval_seconds |
